findings.claim: Removing the `(?=[\s\S]*[\p{Extended_Pictographic}\p{Regional_Indicator}⃣])` lookahead makes the emoji regex accept strings containing no emoji at all, e.g. "123", "#", "*", a lone ZWJ (U+200D), a lone variation selector (U+FE0F), or a bare skin-tone modifier.
findings.rationale: `\p{Emoji_Component}` includes ASCII digits, `#`, `*`, U+200D, U+FE0F, U+20E3 and the skin-tone/hair modifiers. With the anchor lookahead gone, `^[\p{Extended_Pictographic}\p{Emoji_Component}]+$` matches inputs made entirely of these components, so `z.string().emoji()` silently starts validating non-emoji strings — a loosening of validation for all existing callers. High confidence this is a real behavior regression; the retained comment's stated motivation (exponential backtracking from `(A|B)+`) is addressed by the single character class alone and did not require dropping the lookahead.
